definitions.explanation: A Japanese festival held on July 7th celebrating the annual meeting of the deities Orihime and Hikoboshi across the Milky Way.

examples.japanese: {七夕|たなばた}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}→願い事：14621_negaigoto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: I wrote a wish for Tanabata.

examples.japanese: {七夕|たなばた}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{七月|しちがつ}→七月：00667_shichigatsu⟧⟦{七日|なのか}→七日：02927_nanoka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|おこな}われる→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
⟦{子|こ}どもたち→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{七夕|たなばた}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{七夕|たなばた} originates from the Chinese Qixi Festival, combined with Japanese legends. The name literally means 'seventh evening.'

THE LEGEND:
The weaver princess ⟦{織姫|おりひめ}→織姫：25130_orihime⟧ (represented by Vega) and the cowherd ⟦{彦星|ひこぼし}→彦星：26047_hikoboshi⟧ (represented by Altair) are lovers separated by the ⟦{天|あま}の{川|がわ}→天の川：05050_amanogawa⟧ (Milky Way). They are allowed to meet only once a year on this night.

TRADITIONS:
- Writing wishes on ⟦{短冊|たんざく}→短冊：13674_tanzaku⟧ (colored paper strips)
- Hanging decorations on bamboo branches (⟦{笹|ささ}→笹：04407_sasa⟧)
- Making ⟦{七夕飾|たなばたかざ}り→七夕飾り：28962_tanabatakazari⟧ (Tanabata decorations)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{七夕祭|たなばたまつ}り→七夕祭り：25983_tanabatamatsuri⟧: Tanabata festival
- ⟦{七夕飾|たなばたかざ}り→七夕飾り：28962_tanabatakazari⟧: Tanabata decorations
- {七夕|たなばた}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧: the night of Tanabata

REGIONAL VARIATION:
In some regions (notably Sendai), Tanabata is celebrated on August 7th following the old lunar calendar.
